data.argument: The headline growth overstates the durability of the print. Water and wastewater revenue more than doubled, but water deliveries also surged from 76 to 631 acre-feet, making the quarter unusually volume-sensitive; assuming lower deliveries and fading oil-and-gas demand would pressure this key growth engine. Management’s continued-demand outlook is not evidence of contracted volume. Lot sales rose only 19%, well below total revenue growth, while the $14.8 million of expected milestone and finished-lot payments remains forward-looking and dependent on execution and builder absorption. Phase 2E’s 159 planned lots are explicitly paced to absorption, signaling demand remains a constraint. The model left net income, EBITDA, and EPS unchanged and does not quantify downside from lower volumes. Peer read-across is mixed: GWRS supports momentum, but CWCO reported declines.
key_points: Water growth is highly exposed to lower deliveries and oil-and-gas demand.
Forward milestone payments and Phase 2E lots depend on execution and absorption.
Model earnings were unchanged and do not reflect a lower-volume downside case.
assumptions: Water deliveries and related water revenue normalize below the current quarter.
Oil-and-gas demand weakens despite management’s current outlook.
Builder absorption limits the pace of future lot monetization.
